newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-BLUNDELL WINS TORONTO CART RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BLUNDELL WINS TORONTO CART RACE.

text.p: Briton Mark Blundell, driving a Reynard Mercedes-Benz, held off Italian Alessandro Zanardi to win the Toronto CART race by .659 seconds on Sunday.
Blundell led all but two laps of the 95-lap race to earn a second victory in his last three races. He averaged 92.779 mph (149.374 kph).
Andre Ribeiro of Brazil was third 11.874 seconds behind in another Reynard Honda. Michael Andretti of the United States was fourth in a Swift Ford.
Blundell's PacWest Racing team hand not had a CART victory in its four year history. Blundell was one corner away from winning June's Detroit Grand Prix when he ran out of fuel.

With less than 10 laps to go, Zanardi and Blundell started roaring through the 1.721-mile (2.77 km), 11-turn circuit in less than a minute. They went nose-to-tail a number of times, but each time Blundell pulled away.
Pole-sitter Dario Franchitti held the lead for only a few metres. He and Bobby Rahal touched in the first turn and Franchitti spun out. Franchitti dropped to 27th of the 28-car field.
The crash gave Blundell, on the outside of Row 1, the lead.
"I had a good start," said Blundell. "I kept with Dario and wanted to keep him on a tight line. The next thing I saw, Dario was sideways.
"I had to decide whether to go right or left. Luckily I got through. The rest is history."
The middle part of the race was much like a parade, with Blundell holding a lead and none eager to risk passing.

Franchitti, the rookie from Scotland, was the biggest risk-taker, showing some impressive speed and skill, moving all the way back to 11th. He even briefly held the lead on Lap 34 when the leaders pitted. But he crashed out of the race on Lap 39, running 11th at the time.
A record 69,210 fans took in Sunday's event, bringing the total attendance to 166,516 for three days.
